g.text: Only global layers pay for context

path.style: fill: none; stroke: #dc2626; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap: square

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0f172a

font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: Left three: which keys a query may attend to. A sliding window makes the per-layer cache constant in context instead of linear,

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: but evicting the first tokens collapses quality -- models dump surplus attention mass there -- so those slots are kept, either

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: explicitly (attention sinks) or as a learned per-head sink logit. Right: a 48-layer model, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: Interleaving five windowed layers per global layer, as Gemma 3 does, is what makes a 128k context affordable.
